building.name: Talbot-Dutton House
building.completed_conflict: Dated to 1876; the assessor's roll records the parcel as built 1900.

historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 57, Talbot-Dutton House.
Built as a gift from the lumberman William C. Talbot, of Pope & Talbot, to his daughter Mary and her husband Henry Dutton Jr.; Talbot applied for its water service in May 1875.

Bought by Jacob Goldberg, a founder of the grocers Goldberg, Bowen & Co., who added a rear wing on the east side, remodelled the interior and replaced the carriage house with a larger one with a flat upstairs; by the Second World War the house had been divided into several units.

notable_residents.name: Henry Dutton Jr.
notable_residents.detail: Henry Dutton Jr., a director of Pope & Talbot's Puget Mill Company, lived here with his wife Mary from 1876 until his death in 1887; she stayed until her death in 1894.
